stem: A 7-month-old infant has eczema affecting the cheeks with relative sparing of the adjacent facial folds; which term best describes this distribution pattern?
explanation: Headlight sign is the correct term for cheek-predominant infantile eczema with relative sparing of the facial folds. This distribution is a classic bedside pattern in young infants.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because lichenification refers to thickened skin from chronic rubbing or scratching, not this facial distribution pattern.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because headlight sign describes prominent cheek involvement with relative sparing of the surrounding facial folds in infantile eczema.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because excoriation means scratch marks or superficial skin damage, not a named pattern of eczema distribution.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because napkin dermatitis is irritation in the nappy area, not cheek-predominant eczema.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because coloboma is a congenital structural eye defect and is unrelated to eczema distribution.
